# QS-CFW-2490-88 Quality specification - connecting rod CFW-2490-88 (1045)

Revision: Rev C  
Plant: P1  
Parts: CFW-2490-88

Scope
- This quality specification applies to the forging, heat treatment verification, machining interface inspection, and final release inspection for connecting rod CFW-2490-88 produced at Plant P1.
- The document defines acceptance criteria for hardness, bore geometry, and maximum forging mass, and establishes inspection methods, record requirements, and nonconformance handling for those attributes.
- This specification is intended for use by production, quality, heat treat, and machining personnel as the controlling acceptance standard for CFW-2490-88.

Requirements table
- Attribute: Material
  - Requirement: Medium carbon steel nominally supplied as specified for CFW-2490-88 connecting rods.
  - Evidence: Mill test report and incoming material verification record.
- Attribute: Hardness
  - Requirement: The hardness range for connecting rod CFW-2490-88 (CFW-2490-88) is 22-27 HRC.
  - Evidence: Hardness test log entries showing location and reading; equipment calibration certificate traceable to calibration system.
  - Acceptance rule: All measured production samples must fall within the stated hardness range.
- Attribute: Bearing bore diameter
  - Requirement: The bore diameter tolerance for connecting rod CFW-2490-88 (CFW-2490-88) is ±0.02 mm.
  - Evidence: Dimensional inspection reports showing measured bore diameters and tool calibration records.
  - Acceptance rule: Gauged and measured diameters must be within the nominal drawing dimension plus or minus the stated tolerance.
- Attribute: Forging mass
  - Requirement: The maximum forging weight for connecting rod CFW-2490-88 (CFW-2490-88) is 50.1 kg.
  - Evidence: Batch mass report and individual forging weight record.
  - Acceptance rule: Any forging exceeding the stated maximum forging weight must be segregated and dispositioned per nonconformance handling.
- Attribute: Visual and surface condition
  - Requirement: Free from cracks, laps, major laps, and other surface discontinuities that affect fit, function, or safety.
  - Evidence: Visual inspection checklist and NDT records where performed.

Inspection method
- Receiving inspection
  - Verify incoming material documentation and perform visual check for shipment damage. Record material certificates on the incoming material form.
- Hardness verification
  - Location: Verify hardness at specified locations on the rod that represent the critical bearing and shank regions. Use a portable or bench hardness tester validated for HRC scale; record each reading on the hardness test log.
  - Procedure rationale: Hardness control ensures appropriate strength and toughness balance after heat treatment. Sampling should cover representative pieces from each heat to detect process drift.
  - Example entry: Record equipment ID, operator initials, test points, and raw HRC values. If a reading is outside the stated hardness range, follow nonconformance handling.
  - Calibration: Verify tester calibration status prior to use and record calibration reference on the test log.
- Dimensional inspection of bore diameter
  - Measurement method: Measure bore diameters using calibrated internal micrometers, bore gauges, or air gauging where applicable. Verify instruments are within their calibration cycle prior to inspection and document instrument ID.
  - Rationale: The specified bore diameter tolerance directly controls clearance at assembly; adherence prevents premature wear and ensures proper fit to mating components.
  - Example entry: Record nominal drawing diameter, measured value, instrument used, and inspection operator.
  - Acceptance: Values must conform to the stated bore diameter tolerance.
- Forging mass verification
  - Measurement method: Weigh each forging on a calibrated industrial scale and record the mass on the forging mass record.
  - Rationale: Mass control confirms correct material volume and identifies potential leftover flash or incomplete forgings that could affect machining allowance and properties.
  - Acceptance: Any forging exceeding the maximum forging weight must be segregated and evaluated per nonconformance handling.

Nonconformance handling
- Identification and segregation
  - Any part that fails to meet the hardness range, bore diameter tolerance, or maximum forging mass shall be clearly identified and isolated from conforming product. Marking and segregation shall be sufficient to prevent inadvertent use.
- Containment actions
  - Stop shipment of suspect lots. Notify quality control and production supervision immediately. Document the nonconformance on the nonconformance report form and attach supporting inspection records.
- Evaluation and disposition
  - Quality personnel shall evaluate the root cause and extent of nonconformance using available inspection data, process records, and operator interviews. Disposition options include rework if feasible, acceptance with concession following engineering approval, or scrap. The disposition decision must be recorded and signed by authorized personnel.
  - Example scenarios: A hardness value below the specified range may indicate heat-treat cycle deviation; corrective actions may include retest of the batch, adjustment of heat-treat parameters, and reheat where metallurgically acceptable. A bore diameter outside tolerance may be returned to machining if material allowance permits; otherwise, follow scrap disposition.
- Records and corrective action tracking
  - Maintain nonconformance reports, inspection logs, calibration certificates, and disposition records in the document control system. Records shall include a description of the issue, affected quantities, investigation summary, root cause, corrective actions taken, and verification of effectiveness.
  - Rationale: Retaining complete records ensures traceability and supports continuous improvement activities.

Records to keep
- Hardness test logs with equipment identification and operator initials.
- Dimensional inspection reports showing measured bore diameters and instrument calibration references.
- Forging mass records showing individual part weights.
- Incoming material certificates and mill test reports.
- Nonconformance reports and disposition records.

Notes and rationale
- The specified hardness, bore tolerance, and maximum forging mass are primary acceptance criteria for CFW-2490-88 given their direct impact on performance and interchangeability. The inspection methods are selected to provide objective, verifiable evidence for acceptance decisions. Records generated during inspection and nonconformance handling are mandatory for traceability and corrective action verification.
